title: Canonical maps for compact-support diagonal integration
statement: Let \(A\) be a finite commutative ring, \(f:X\to Y\) a proper morphism of schemes, and \(W=X\times_Y X\), with projections \(p_1,p_2\) and diagonal \(\Delta\). Work in the ordinary unbounded small-etale derived categories of \(A\)-modules, with the tensor and compact-support functors of [def-pur-td-datum] and the canonical pullback comparisons of [def-sfb-etale-coordinate-trace-data]. Write \(F=Rf_!\), \(P_i=Rp_{i!}\), \(U=R\Delta_!\mathbf1_X\), \(H_B(K)=B\otimes f^*K\), and \(E_B(M)=p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*B\). Define the outside-first projection \(\pi_{g,M,V}:M\otimes Rg_!V\simeq Rg_!(g^*M\otimes V)\) by symmetry, the canonical projection formula, and pushed symmetry. Define \(C_B:P_2E_B\simeq H_BF\) by sndProjectionIso followed by the inverse symmetry, and \(D:FP_2\simeq FP_1\) by inverse composition for \(p_2,f\), congruence \(fp_2=fp_1\), and composition for \(p_1,f\). For \(t:FB\to\mathbf1_Y\), let \(\epsilon_t(K)\) be inverse projectionIso at \((B,K)\), then \(t\otimes\mathrm{id}\), then the left unitor. Let \(\beta_1\) be exchange for the flipped self-pullback square, and \(\beta_2\) the unflipped exchange. For \(e:B\simeq f^*L\), define \(c_e:p_1^*B\simeq p_2^*B\) using \(e\) and the equality of the maps to \(Y\). Put \(t_1=\beta_1^{-1};f^*t;\mathrm{unit}\) and \(t_2=P_2(c_e^{-1});\beta_2^{-1};f^*t;\mathrm{unit}\). Identify \(H_BK\simeq f^*(L\otimes K)\) by tensoring \(e\) with identity and the inverse pullback-tensor comparison; its coordinate comparison is \(c_H:p_1^*H_BK\simeq p_2^*H_BK\). Let \(\alpha_i:\mathrm{Id}\simeq P_iR\Delta_!\) be the canonical identity/composition comparisons for \(p_i\Delta=\mathrm{id}\). For \(\delta:U\to p_2^*B\), define \(I_\delta:\mathrm{Id}\to P_2E_B\) by idIsoDiagonalSnd, pushed diagonalIso, and the pushed tensor of \(\delta\) followed by symmetry. The diagonal unit is \(I_\delta;C_B\), the counit is \(\epsilon_t\), and Integrals is \(\alpha_i(\mathbf1_X);P_i(\delta);t_i=\mathrm{id}\) for both coordinates. Semicolons denote composition in application order. These are explicit canonical composites without proof holes. The original exchangeFirst, coordinate, diagonalFirst, traceFirst, traceSecond, Integrals and counit definitions move verbatim. The unit is the same canonical composite reassociated as insertion followed by comparisonIso; comparison gives its components. The right unitor \(\rho_M:M\otimes\mathbf1_X\simeq M\) is the canonical right unitor. The component \(I_\delta(M)\) has domain \(M\) and codomain \(P_2(E_B(M))\); it is the component of the specified insertion natural transformation.

def comparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (B M : DerivedCategoryModule A X) :
    (push A (pullback.snd f f)).obj (kernel A f B M) ≅
      (CoordinateTrace.pull A f ⋙ (derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj B).obj ((push A
        f).obj M)
